### 2026-10-07 – October 7th :

**1.5h**

October 7th :

    I researched what  SCL, SDA and GPIO are to  help me understand what  the connections in my tutorial guide meant . I understood that SCL is the I²C clock line and SDA carries data between devices. I also learned that GPIO pins can be used for different inputs and outputs.

### 2026-10-09 – Today,I wanted to make the starbie bit unique so I thought of changing the original tamagotchi thing to a mini study tool. To do this I added a  RGB LED, buzzer circuit and LDR light sensor, with  my

**5h**

Today,I wanted to make the starbie bit unique so I thought of changing the original tamagotchi thing to a mini study tool. To do this I added a  RGB LED, buzzer circuit and LDR light sensor, with  my newly the updated XIAO ESP32-C3 microcontroller for the schematic .

I used signal names such as  labels such as Btn1, Btn2, DHT11_DATA, LDR_SIG, SCL and SDA to make the connections between components easier to follow.

My next step is to check the  every pin and  components  with the Electrical Rules Checker (ERC) before moving on to footprints and PCB layout.

**TL;DR:**  I thought to make the starbie unique by changing the tamagotchi idea to a mini study buddy. To do that I updated the  schematic in KiCad by adding RGB LED, buzzer and light sensor along with the original OLED, MPU6050 and DHT11 sections with the XIAO ESP32-C3.

### 2026-10-10 – October 10th

**3h**

October 10th

Today, I continued working on my PCB in KiCad by working on footprint assignments, symbol fields and fixing warnings in the schematic.  I did this to get prepared  for later to work in the PCB Editor.

I first opened the Assign Footprints tool to assign suitable footprints to the components in my design. Then I reviewed the available footprint libraries to find suitable options for the components.

I  then checking the symbol fields so that the component references, values and footprint assignments would be clear and consistent.

At last I ran the ERC to find any errors.

My next step is to transfer the schematic into the PCB editor. I will then begin arranging the components and planning the board layout.

TL;DR:I continued working on  the schematic in KiCad by assigning component footprints, reviewing symbol fields and working on fixing schematic warnings before moving on to the physical PCB layout.

### 2026-10-11 – Today, I continued developing the Starbie project in KiCad transfering my schematics editor to the pcb editor. Once had assigned footprints to the components, I imported it into the PCB editor  to lay

**4h**

Today, I continued developing the Starbie project in KiCad transfering my schematics editor to the pcb editor. Once had assigned footprints to the components, I imported it into the PCB editor  to layout.

I first imported the schematics from the editor to the pcb editor to position  and experimente the layout of the main components, including the XIAO ESP32-C3, DHT11 environmental sensor, push buttons, buzzer, RGB LED, LDR and resistors. Then once I have made the perfect layout I started to work on the copper tracks to connect the components according to the schematic. I also inspected individual pad properties, including pad sizes, hole dimensions and net assignments, to make sure all the holes are in the right size.

Once I finished I used  KiCad's 3D viewer. This allowed me to see how the components would look when assembled on the board and check their physical placement.

TL;DR:I continued working on  the Starbie PCB in KiCad by importing and arranging component footprints, beginning the copper routing process, inspecting pad properties and viewing the board in 3D to check the physical component layout.

### 2026-10-11 – Today, I uploaded the initial  firmware scaffold to my GitHub repository and worked on writing the README to explain the project, its hardware components . I organised the firmware code for the XIAO E

**3h**

Today, I uploaded the initial  firmware scaffold to my GitHub repository and worked on writing the README to explain the project, its hardware components . I organised the firmware code for the XIAO ESP32-C3 and documented the GPIO assignments based on my KiCad schematic. I also outlined the features I plan to implement during Build Week, including the OLED interface, study timer, environmental sensors and user controls. The firmware is still an initial version, and I will develop and test the complete functionality during Build Week. I have also uploaded my Gerber, Schematic components, Pcb 3d view and etc.
